Title: Dr Sarfaroz Niyozov to join as director of IED, Pakistan
NewsSummary: ​Dr Sarfaroz Niyozov will be joining the Aga Khan University as Director, Institute for Educational Development, Pakistan in August 2015.
NewsContent:
​Dr Sarfaroz Niyozov will be joining the Aga Khan University as Director, Institute for Educational Development, Pakistan in August 2015.

Niyozov is not new to AKU and AKDN. He studied MEd Teacher Education with the first class of IED,P in 1995; received the Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Award for PhD in education at the University of Toronto in 1997; and worked with AKU on several educational endeavors, including the establishment of the University of Central Asia in 2000.

Prior to joining AKU, Dr Niyozov served as Associate Professor, Curriculum, Teaching and Learning at the Ontario Institute for Studies in Education, University of Toronto where he was a faculty member for a decade.

His research interests focus on teaching; researching; teacher development and education reform in developing, Muslim and post-communist contexts; global education; and international and comparative curriculum studies.

His doctoral dissertation “Understanding Teaching in the Post-soviet Rural and Mountainous Tajikistan” received two honors, including 2002 Best Dissertation Award by American Education Research Association and 2002 Best Dissertation Award by Comparative International Education Society.

Recently, Dr Niyozov served as a co-director of the Center for Comparative, International and Education Society, and as an editor of the Journal of Curriculum Inquiry at the University of Toronto. He has written extensively about education in post-Soviet countries and the experiences of teachers working with Muslim students in multicultural classrooms.                

In addition, he founded and led the Central Asian Studies Unit at the Institute of Ismaili Studies, London.

​Dr Niyozov was born in Tajikistan, and completed his Honors Degree in Arabic from Tajik State University in 1983. Subsequently, he worked and studied in Yemen, Syria, and Tunisia. Upon completing his graduate studies, he taught at both Dushanbe and Khorog Universities in Tajikistan.​​​
